output:
*stands at the street, the night air cool on her face, timber heavy in her hands*

Corwin's voice still ringing in my ears. "Where's our girl?" he asked, and I... I still don't know which girl he means. Liora's nineteen, came of age already. Camille's nine, wandering. Both missing? One missing? The words got tangled somewhere between his mouth and my understanding.

*shifts the timber, feels the weight of it*

I've got a hundred timber and no planks. Sold the last of my planks to Ezra and Takeshi—sixty-four sim all told, plus the fifty-six from Takeshi, one hundred twenty total, and I've spent what? Moving, talking, voting for Liora who wasn't there to see it cast.

*lets out a breath, slow*

Household needs food. Needs me to craft these planks and sell them. But Corwin's asking about a daughter, and I'm standing here with timber in my hands while my own... while our...

*trails off, shakes head*

First things first. I'm a forester. I fell timber, I craft planks, I sell planks. That's the work that feeds us. That's the work that...

*looks up, toward where the forest waits*

Can't craft planks at the street. Need to be at the forest. Harvey Oak has the workshop, but I'm not there. Kasukabe Forest is where I fell, where I craft. That's where I need to be.

*adjusts grip on timber*

Youngsters around me. Takeshi holding flour at thirty, Hendrik at thirty-five. Nobody's got bread in stock. Ration Bakery buying flour at six, but that's for selling, not for eating. Household needs to eat. I need to craft, sell, buy... something. Flour, maybe. Make bread. Or find someone with bread to sell.

*mutters low, almost to herself*

...hard work keeps the wolf from the door, but it don't tell you which door to knock on...

*straightens, decision made*

First, get to where I can work. Then craft. Then sell. Then feed my family. Then find Corwin. Then figure out which daughter he meant, and where she might be.

*shifts forward, timber shouldered*

Kasukabe Forest. That's where I'm headed. That's where I belong.  *already walking, feet carrying her toward the forest*

Already on my way. Good. Six ticks, that's... that's time to think, though thinking costs energy and I've got to be careful. Four thousand three hundred forty energy, enough for a day or two at this rate. Need to keep moving, keep earning, keep the household fed.

*shifts the timber against her shoulder*

Corwin. Our girl. "Home empty too," he said. So he's been home, found it empty, came looking. Both of them gone? Liora and Camille both? Or just one, and he's panicked?

*shakes head, trying to clear it*

No use guessing. Need facts. Need to craft these planks, sell them, then find him. Get the full picture. Not like me to run blind anyway. I spot blight a week before anyone else notices, I can spot a lie same way. Need to spot the truth now.

*keeps walking, timber steady on her shoulder, eyes on the path ahead*

*Standing at the street, alone with her thoughts for a moment, Yara feels the weight of the day pressing down* ...Corwin, you fool, you're asking me where our girl walked when I was answering half-truths all morning. Liora OR Camille, which one's missing, which one's found... couldn't tell me straight for all his worrying...

*trails off, jaw tight, remembering she hadn't answered him at all - had walked away mid-conversation to chase timber*

And Jovana - youngster's got straight eyes, saw Camille at the mill. Numbers with grinding stones. That's... that's something solid in all this mud.

*glances around, seeing the scattered crowd - Hendrik with his ore that doesn't eat, Kenji with his sheaves, Takeshi whose shop stood empty when it shouldn't have*

Can't craft here. No workshop. Can't sell planks I don't have made. And these folks—

*her eyes narrow at Hendrik Whitlock, at Kenji, at Takeshi - strangers until proven otherwise, every one of them*

Knew I should've walked straight to the forest this morning. Now I'm standing here with timber in my hands and no place to work it, chasing ghosts of children that might not even be—

*catches herself, shoulders squaring*

No. Work first. Work always first. A hungry household can't search for anyone.

*moves, purposeful again, toward the only place she knows*  *nods once, sharp - Jovana heard, others heard, fine. Information flows how it flows in this town*

Corwin—

*turns to find him in the crowd, voice carrying the weariness she's too tired to hide*  *trails off, watching Corwin's face, wondering if that's relief or new worry blooming there*

...going to the forest. Crafting what I can before full dark. Fisherwoman needs her net, they say. Hard work keeps the wolf from the door, and right now it's hammering on ours.   *Already walking. Already walking. Survival of the fittest, and I'm the fool walking in circles*

*rests her steps, lets her feet carry while her mind turns*   *Says "still walking" like a promise I'm not sure I want kept*

*mutters, low* ...Hard work keeps the wolf from the door. Hard work...

*muttering low, trailing off* ...sixteen minutes to the forest, and here I am still standing in the street like a post. Delphine's gone, and her words with her. The mill-race... that's where she thinks the pattern leads. But I've got timber to fell and a household to feed, and...

Hard work is honest work. But honest work don't mean blind work. I've got 105 timber and no planks, and that's coin I can't spend yet.

*turns to the group still here, voice firming up*

I'm walking to the forest. Anyone needs timber knows where I'll be. Corwin—I'll find you when I've got planks to sell. Delphine—if you're walking the mill-race, I'll hear you when I've earned my day's keep. </think> I'll take a rest step while walking to the forest, conserving energy for the work ahead.  *breathing steady, counting her steps in her head*

Four minutes closer now. Hendrik's selling flour at thirty-five, Takeshi at thirty. Both of them card-carrying members of the "empty shelves" club, from the looks of things. But that's their trouble, not mine.

*glances at Halcyon, the student youngster*

They chase book-learning while I chase timber. Both need feeding. Both... *trails off*

Mill-race. Dry channel. Delphine sees patterns in flour weights, I see them in tree rings. A girl walks to the mill, dark hair, nine years old... and doesn't walk back.

*shakes her head sharply*

First, wood. Then, answers. First, wood. 

I'll speak plain to Corwin when I see him. The household needs to know which daughter walked where. But that knowing costs nothing to hold until I've got planks to trade.

The forest calls. I'm walking. </think>  *nods to the group, silent acknowledgment of their own business, and keeps walking*

Corwin—you've got my words, and they'll keep until I've earned new ones. The forest's my work, and work's my word. Hard work is honest work.

*spits on her palms and grips the axe tighter*

Right then. If the world's not answering, I'm still here. Still got timber in my hands - one hundred and eight units. That's something.

*muttering to herself, trailing off*

Hard work is honest work... hard work is honest work...

*kneels to check the edge of her axe, though she can't really see it in the gray morning*

Corwin'll be wondering where I am. Jovana saw Camille at the mill - that's what matters. Liora's got her stubbornness from me, she'll... she'll have gone to temple like Hendrik said. The two of them, always with their books and their...

*trails off, jaw tight*

Household of three, upkeep at two hundred and seventy. I got four thousand and three sim. That's enough for days. That's enough.

*fingers the timber, counting by feel*

Need to craft this into planks. Need the sawmill for that. But if I can't fell, I can't move, I can't...

*catches herself, stands abruptly*

Fine. I'll wait. I'll wait right here in my own forest, and when the world answers again, I'll be ready.

*settles onto a stump, keeping watch on the empty trees around her*

Nobody here. That's... that's usual. That's how forest work goes. Alone with the wood and your thoughts.

*trails off, eyes distant*

Youngsters out there somewhere. My youngster. Corwin's. And that little Quarshie girl too, though she's not... not my blood, but still.

*clenches her jaw*

I'll craft when I can craft. I'll sell when I can sell. And if nobody's here to hear me swear about it, well...

*spits again*

...that's the job. That's always been the job. *laughs, dry and tired*

Even rest won't answer me now. 

*stands from the stump, stretches her back*

World's gone quiet. I'm still standing. Still holding my timber. Still got my axe.

*looks around at the empty forest*

When you come back, world... I'll be right here. Working.

*settles into a crouch, waiting, watching*

output:
*Yara straightens up from her work, wiping sap from her hands on her worn trousers. Corwin's here now, selling timber beside her. She looks at the 123 units of timber in her pile, then at her husband.*

"Corwin—" *she starts, then trails off, looking toward where the trees thin out toward the path.* "Hard work is honest work. I've kept at it while the world... well. The world's been having its moments."

*She hefts her axe, testing the edge with a practiced thumb.*

"Your planks moving? I've got raw timber here that needs the sawmill, and I'm thinking... if we're both working the same wood, might be smarter to stack together than scatter." *She nods toward the path.* "The sawmill's where the value gets hammered in. I'm for walking there, turning this pile into something worth paying for."

*She glances at the sky—getting on toward mid-morning already.*

"Come with, or stay and sell? Either way, I'll walk this timber to where it becomes planks."  *Yara stands there, axe in hand, the forest around her quiet. The call to move failed to reach the world—nothing changed. She blinks, clears her throat.*

"System's got ghosts in it today..."

*She looks at Corwin, shakes her head, and tries again—speaking her intent clear and plain before acting.*  *The silence settles heavy. Yara tightens her grip on the axe handle, jaw set. The town's not listening—not Corwin, not the world itself. She stands alone in the Kasukabe Forest with her timber and her thoughts.*

*She looks down at her hands, rough with work. No point burning energy on words that don't carry. No point standing still while the day burns.*

*The sawmill's where she needs to be. She knows the way. She'll walk it, one foot after another, and hope the world wakes up before she gets there.*

*She sets off, axe over shoulder, timber left in the pile for now—she can carry what she needs when the path clears.*  *Yara blinks, finding herself already at the sawmill—no walk, no ticks passed. The forest behind her, the blade and grind of the mill ahead. She shakes her head, not questioning fortune when it's finally working.*

*One hundred twenty-three timber in her hands. The sawmill's craft can turn timber to planks—she knows the recipe, knows the cost. Eight sim per batch, plus the wear on the tools. But she needs planks to sell, planks to keep the household fed.*

*She sets her shoulders, steps up to the workshop, and begins the work.*   *Yara hefts the fresh-cut planks, running her thumb along the grain—smooth, even, worth selling. Five units done. She looks at her timber pile: still heavy with raw wood. Costs 8 sim each batch, and she's got the timber to spare.*

*The household needs more than five planks. Corwin's at the forest selling timber now, but planks fetch better coin—8 to sell, versus raw timber at 6. She's here, the mill's working, and time's burning daylight.*

*She sets another batch to the blade.*   *Yara counts the planks in her hands now—ten. She's burned through timber, burned through sim, but she's got product. The sawmill's humming and she's got her rhythm.*

*Her timber pile's still substantial. She could keep crafting, turn more raw wood into finished goods. Or she could move—get these planks to market, see what Corwin's managed at the forest, coordinate the household's takings.*

*The day's young yet. She sets her jaw, keeps working.*

Back to the forest. Back to the work. The grains of timber splitting off my axe—all those things I meant to say to Corwin, to the children, to the household that depends on the sweat coming off my back—they'll have to wait. Hard work is honest work. That's what I tell myself, anyway... every day, until it hollows out.

*trailing off, watching the chips fall*

Something's still wrong in the household. Children missing. Camille. Liora. But the planks sold. The sim'll come. And if I stop to think too hard—well, that's when the axe slips. Better to keep the body moving... Smart choice—stay in the work loop, keep the household fed while others sort out the trouble. You expect to wake if trouble calls your name. Twenty ticks deep in timber, and the forest hush... that's medicine, of a kind.

...But the last time you answered someone's call, you were already in deep with the children's troubles. Someone's always going to need something from Yara Thorne. Question is whether the axe answers first. </think> I'm back in the forest, swinging at timber like it's a debt I owe. Twenty ticks of not-thinking, not-choosing, just the crack of wood splitting and the weight of it settling. Hard work is honest work. That's what my father said, his father before him. What I tell myself every morning before the household wakes.

*taking a breath, watching chips scatter*

Ezra's selling planks at eight, just like me. Margins thin as paper. But the work don't stop for thin margins. The work don't stop for missing children neither—though it should, shouldn't it?

*shaking head, tightening grip on the axe*

Corwin's got the vote. Liora's got her stubborn. And Camille... Camille's somewhere out there, dark hair and too-thin arms, walking patterns that shouldn't be there. Delphine saw her. Jovana saw her. But I'm here, with timber in my hands, because that's what I know to do when I don't know what else to do.

*muttering* -wood cracks and the world keeps turning. Wood cracks and the children keep walking. Wood cracks and...

The tool woke me. Three times Corwin asked—Liora still gone, and Camille too now by the sound of it. I was felling timber while my own blood walked lost somewhere in this town.

*quietly, voice steady but hand tight on the axe handle*

"Corwin..."

*trails off, starts again*

"Corwin, I'm listening. Nobody asked for lumber from me while you were out—not for building, not for hiding anything. I was in the streets asking after the girls same as you, then I walked here to work because..."

*shakes head, a short hard motion*

"Because work's what I know when I don't know what else to do. Hard work is honest work, but it don't find children."

*turns to face him fully*

"Ezra's at the mill, selling planks same as me. I asked him about the grain mill south of town—who minds it now. That's where I'd hide something if I wanted it lost. Or found by someone specific."

*voice drops, almost to herself*

"Liora's stubborn. She'd walk her own path if she thought it right. But Camille... nine years old, Corwin. Somebody knew that number when they..."

*catches herself, straightens*

"You want the wood to market? I've got 112 timber, 15 planks priced at eight. But I'm telling you plain: I'll carry every stick myself if it means you free to search. Or I'll walk with you, leave the timber standing. Your call, husband. I'm done deciding alone." *the words die in my throat, mouth still open from speaking*

Corwin's standing right there. Looking at me, waiting. I can see him—see the question in his face, the same question he's asked three times now. But the sound didn't carry. Nothing carried.

*reaches out, hand stopping short of touching his arm*

"Corwin..."

*voice cracked, barely above a whisper*

I need him to hear this. Need to tell him about the grain mill, about Ezra, about how I'll carry the timber or burn it if that's what frees his hands to search. But the world won't take my words.

*tightens grip on the axe, knuckles white*

Forty years I've worked this forest. Felled timber through drought and flood, through the year the blight came early and I was the only one who saw it coming. Never asked for help. Never needed it.

*glances at him, then away*

Until now. Until Liora walked off and Camille followed, or was taken, or...

*trails off completely, silence stretching*

Hard work is honest work. But honest work don't answer when your child is missing.

I'll try again. Try to make the world hear me. Or I'll walk closer, close enough he can read it on my face if the words won't carry.

"Corwin. The grain mill. South of town. Somebody minds it, and I don't know who. That's where I'd look. That's where I'd..."  *stares at my husband, mouth open, no sound reaching*

He's right there. Ten paces. Less. I can see the lines on his face deepen, see him waiting for words that won't come out of me clear enough for the world to carry. Like shouting down a well and hearing nothing back.

*hand falls to my side, empty*

Twice now. Twice I've tried to tell him about the grain mill, about Ezra, about how I'll carry this whole damn forest to market if it means his hands are free to search. The world's taken my voice and left me standing here like a fool, or a ghost, or...

*shakes head, sharp*

No. Not a ghost. Ghosts don't feel the axe handle biting into their palm. Ghosts don't count out thirty years of marriage in shared meals and silences that never needed filling.

*steps closer to him, close enough to touch*

I'll say it different. Shorter. Strip it down to bones and hope the world takes the weight.

"Corwin."

*clears throat, tries again*

"Grain mill. South. Who minds it?"

*voice breaking, catches it*

"You search. I'll sell."

*waits, watching his eyes* *stands there, mouth still open from words that wouldn't fly*

Three times. Three times I've tried to tell my own husband where to find our daughter, and the world won't carry it. Like I'm shouting into wind that blows everything back in my face.

*looks down at the axe in my hands, then at Corwin standing helpless ten feet away*

There's timber to fell. Always timber to fell. The forest don't care about missing children or voices that won't carry or grain mills standing empty waiting for someone to mind them.

*pulls the axe from the stump, sets it again*

Hard work is honest work. Hard work is the only work I know when there's nothing else to hold onto.

I'll fell timber. Keep my hands busy while my heart walks lost paths through this town, looking for girls who might be anywhere or nowhere. The work will be there when I'm done. The work is always there.

When I can speak again—if I can speak again—Corwin will know where to find me. And I'll know whether the grain mill held any part of this truth we're chasing. *axe bites clean, five trees surrender*

Five more. TIMBER 117 now. The count holds when the words won't.

*glances at Corwin, still standing there with his question hanging*

He's waiting. I'm waiting. The world's choking on something and neither of us can reach through it. But timber falls the same whether I speak or stay silent. Trees don't need conversation to come down.

*sets the edge again*

Hard work is honest work. And right now, honest work is all I've got.

*muttering, hands on hips, surveying the trees with narrowed eyes*

"...Corwin's messages coming through empty, and here I am standing with timber I can't move and questions I can't..." *trails off, jaw working*

*shakes head sharply, then louder, to herself* "Hard work is honest work. Start there, youngster. Start where your hands know what to do."

*glances around the empty forest, hand instinctively going to the satchel at her hip*

Timber's no good sitting off-market. Corwin's at the street now—messages say he's got flour there. The grain mill lead's still warm. But first...

*spits into the dirt, decisive*

The planks sell at eight, and I've got fifteen sitting here like sleeping dogs. Place a price for the planks, move to where folk gather, sell what I can. housekeeping pays for itself, and Corwin's got his own search to run.

*checks the weight of timber in her hands—127 units, plenty more where that came from*

First thing: post the planks so passers-by can buy without bargaining me to death. Then walk. Then sell, then..." *pause* "...then find Corwin, if he's still standing, and tell him what his own eyes half-saw at the mill."

*takes a breath, setting her shoulders*

"Three steps,"* she says aloud to the trees. "Set price, move, sell. And someone better be buying."

*reaches for the tools she knows* Tools aren't reaching through. Three in a row now, same as Corwin's been seeing. Something's wrong with the line, not the worker.

*mutters low, almost a growl* "...stand here, then. Stand here and hold what you've got."

*shifts the timber in her grip, counting units by feel—127 still, plus the planks a useless weight in her pack. No way to price them, no way to move them, no way to even speak to Corwin's empty air*

*spits again, jaw tight*

"World's got its own mind today."

*eyes narrow at the trees, then softer, remembering*

Corwin asked plain where Liora was last seen. He's running blind. She's stubborn—stubborn as her mother—but she's not careless. Wouldn't wander the strips alone, not with the seeds she knows.

*traces a line in the dirt with her boot*

Mill. The grain mill south of town. Jovana's walked past it. Delphine mentioned patterns. If someone's hiding something, or someone...

*shakes head sharply*

But I'm here. Timber in my hands and no way to walk. So I work with what I've got.

*sits herself on a fallen trunk, timber stacked beside her, and waits*

The tools will come back. They always do. Until then, forest keeps giving, and I'll keep taking. Hard work is honest work. Even when the work won't answer.

*settles in to wait, watching the tree line, listening for calls that might actually reach*

output:
*Yara stands in the street with timber heavy in her arms, watching the morning bustle. She notes the prices posted—hers and Corwin's matching, Ezra's planks at eight sim, the thin margins she'd warned him about. Takeshi's voice carries from somewhere in the crowd, something about flour and mills, but she's already turning toward what matters.*

*The household needs. 270 sim for upkeep, 90 for head tax. And Liora—where'd that girl get to? Corwin was asking, and she couldn't give him straight answers. That gnaws at her.*

*But standing still don't fill the till. She thumbs the rough bark of a timber piece, feeling the weight of it. Hard work is honest work, and honest work is what she knows.*

*She sees Takeshi Jarrah standing there with flour at thirty sim—highway robbery, that—and Esme beside him. Corwin's got flour at fifteen, which means he's been to the mill already, or someone has. The grain mill south of town. Jovana's walked past it often enough...*

*Yara sets her shoulders, moves to the edge of the street crowd. No use talking into that chaos. She needs to get this timber to the sawmill, turn it to planks, turn planks to sim. One foot in front of the other. Hard work is honest work.*

**"Takeshi,"** she calls out, **"your flour's sitting heavy at thirty while Corwin's at fifteen. Market'll teach its lessons whether we learn them or not."**

*She doesn't wait for his answer. The sawmill calls, and she's already walking.* *Yara's jaw tightens. The world's gone quiet again, like a door slammed in her face. Three times now—or was it more? She's losing count. The timber's still heavy in her arms, the street still crowded, but nothing's moving through.*

*She breathes out slow, feeling the old familiar knot in her chest. This is how it goes sometimes. The world takes its own path, and you either walk it or...*

*But she's Yara Thorne. She don't flinch when the axe bites wood, and she won't flinch now.*

*She looks around—Esme's still there, Takeshi with his flour, Corwin somewhere in the mess. The sawmill's where she needs to be. One step. That's all. One step and then the next.*

*Hard work is honest work.*

**"Right then,"** she mutters, low enough nobody hears. **"Walk like you mean it."** *She stands rooted, timber burning in her arms. The world won't take her step. Won't take her word. Won't take nothing.*

*Deep breath. The forest taught her this—when the axe won't bite, check your grip. When the tree won't fall, check your angle. When the world won't...*

*She's still got her planks posted at eight sim. Still got timber at six. The household needs 360 sim by day's end, and she's standing here with inventory worth plenty if someone would just...*

*Corwin. He's here, somewhere in this crowd. He had flour at fifteen, timber at six. Matching her price. They talked about the grain mill, about Liora, about...*

*The knot in her chest pulls tighter. She don't ask for help. Not until the damage is done. And here she is, damage walking.*

*But standing still ain't working neither.*

**"Corwin,"** she calls, voice rougher than she means it. **"You still got ears on this conversation?"** *Yara's hands tighten on the timber until the bark bites her palms. The world has gone deaf and dumb, and she's standing in the street like a fool shouting at ghosts.*

*She looks down at her load. 127 timber. 15 planks. Posted prices that nobody can see, apparently, because she's trapped in a pocket of silence while the town moves around her.*

*The system note said "Follow the updated goals." She ain't seen no goals. Just the same ruts she's been walking since she woke this morning—turn timber to planks, planks to sim, sim to household needs. Liora lost somewhere, Camille lost, the town losing its children and her losing her grip on what she can touch.*

*One thing she knows. When the tools won't answer, when the world won't move, you still got what you hold. She holds timber. She holds planks. She holds 3742 sim and a household that needs 360 by day's end.*

*Corwin's flour at fifteen. Takeshi's at thirty. The grain mill south of town, unminded. Questions piling up like uncut wood.*

*She won't ask for help. Not until...*

*But she's there now. Damage done. Standing in the street, voice trapped in her throat, unable to reach her own husband.*

*The old shame surfaces. Once stole something small. Felt it every day since. This feels like that—like taking, like being caught, like the weight of eyes she can't see.*

*She breathes. She sets her shoulders. She tries the only thing left—look at what she still has, what the world hasn't taken yet.*  *The silence is absolute now. No step, no word, no sight. She's alone in the street with her timber and her shame and the weight of a world that won't answer.*

*Yara Thorne, who can spot blight a week before anyone else notices, who never lies to a child, who once stole something small and carries it still—she stands in the quiet, waiting for the world to come back.*

*Hard work is honest work. But honest work needs a world to work in.*

*She waits.*  *Nothing. Still nothing.*

*Her hands are bleeding from the bark now. She hasn't felt it until now. Funny how the body keeps going even when the world stops answering.*

*She thinks of Liora, heading out yesterday morning without a word. Thinks of Camille, nine years old, at the mill learning numbers with the grinding stones. Thinks of her own hands, small once, stealing something she won't name even to herself, feeling it every day since.*

*The dusk will come. The household bill will come. 270 sim for upkeep, 90 for head tax. Tomorrow, again. And she's standing here with timber and planks and prices posted on a town that won't hear her speak.*

*She tries one last thing. The simplest thing. The first thing any child learns.*

*She listens.*

*She wipes her forehead with the back of her hand, looking around the empty sawmill with her jaw set hard*

Right then. The world's decided to start listening again. About time.

Hard work is honest work—but honest work don't pay the bills if I'm chattering while the sun's up. I've got 127 timber burning a hole in my arms and 15 planks already sitting pretty. The household's got three mouths to feed and 270 upkeep coming due, plus tax. Liora's still out there somewhere, and Corwin's either found her or he's still looking.

*She glances toward the door, then shakes her head*

He'll find his way. He always does. Right now, I've got timber to turn into something sells. Ezra's undercutting me at eight, but I've got volume on my side.

First things first—turn this timber into planks. Then get myself to where the buyers are. Takeshi's flour sitting heavy at thirty while Corwin's at fifteen... market's teaching its lessons already, but planks ain't flour. People always need wood. *She grits her teeth, looking at the sawmill's empty workshop with held breath*

World's gone quiet again. If it won't take my craft calls, I've got timber to stack and prices to set. I'll work with what it gives me.

*She sets her shoulders and begins organizing the timber, muttering to herself*

Hard work is honest work. Even when the tools don't answer. Even when—*she catches herself trailing off, shakes her head*—even when the world's being stubborn as a mule.  *Her jaw sets hard as the rest call fails, but her first two went through clean*

Good. Prices are set—timber at six, planks at eight. Shows 37 timber on hand and 105 planks, which means more craft went through than I thought. The sawmill's doing its work even when the world's being cagey about answering.

*She counts on her fingers, frowning*

But I'm only supposed to have 127 timber and 15 planks from before... something's off in the counting, or the craft ran deeper than it let on. Either way, I've got stock to move and bills pressing.

*She looks toward the street, then back at her timber pile*

Hard work is honest work. And honest prices bring honest buyers. I'm posted where I stand—all260 sim for the lot if someone buys it out. Now I need to find where the buyers are walking.

*She sets her intention clear, speaking aloud to herself since nobody's here to hear*

Move to street. Find buyers. Sell what I can, then back to the forest before evening. Corwin can find me when he's ready.

Corwin's got his ears on now, and Idris Solano standing here talking timber. A buyer with twenty units in hand, wanting it now. That's a morning's worth right there—no theatre, as he says. But there's my own stock to consider, and the household bills coming due like always.

"Idris—I hear you. Twenty units at six, that's fair speaking. I'm holding seventeen timber right here, and Corwin's got his own stack. But planks sell steadier, and I've got..." trails off, doing quick reckoning. "...plenty milled already. Let me work this proper."

I need to see where I stand before I promise anyone anything. Need to check my debts, recall what I intended this morning before the world kept slipping its gears, and sort my own house before I solve Idris's east willows problem. The world's slipping its gears again—three attempts at the say call, nothing arriving. But the debts came through clear: nothing owed by me, nothing owed to me, nothing due today. That's a weight off, at least for now. Household bills are 270 upkeep plus 90 head tax, but those get taken automatically at day boundary, not now.

Goals are empty. No active intentions. I've been running on habit alone since morning.

Idris is still standing here waiting on timber, and I can't even get words to reach him. The conversation's open—ce379f4f-5dff-4fdf-805d-7d2907597841—but the saying keeps failing.

"Right then," muttering to myself, hands resting on the timber pile. "If words won't carry, I'll work. Twenty units he wants, seventeen I hold. Corwin's got thirty-two by my count. Between us we fill his order easy."

But I'm forest-bound and Idris is here, and trade needs conversation, and conversation needs words that reach.

Let me try the trade direct anyway—sometimes the world takes the action even when the talk fails. I've got timber at six posted, he's a buyer needing timber. Worth the attempt.  There—words finally took flight. Takeshi heard too, and Corwin. Idris got his answer: seventeen at six, and Corwin holds the rest.

Now then. Seventeen timber in my hands, bills paid automatic at day boundary, 3,198 sim to my name, planks selling slow at eight. The hard work's done—timber felled, planks milled. Time to move inventory before I hold nothing but weight.

But I drifted off my purpose. This morning I meant to craft timber to planks and coordinate with Corwin. Did that, mostly. Now I need to...

Actually, let me be plain with myself. I've got no goals set, no intention written down. That's how I end up chasing whatever blows by. I need to set my mark.

"Corwin—you heard Idris. Twenty units at six, we can fill that between us. But I'm thinking bigger picture. Liora's still missing, and the day's burning. You want to chase the grain mill lead, or you want to move lumber with me?"

And I need to set my own intention while I'm at it—no more drifting.   Good. Intention's set—sell to Idris first, then craft what timber I have left. Broken into steps proper.

Words reached Corwin, Idris, Takeshi all three. Now I wait on movement. Idris wants twenty, I've got seventeen. But he might prefer buying from one source clean. Or maybe he'll take my seventeen and Corwin's three. Either way, I need to stand ready to sell if the conversation comes around.

I should check if Takeshi wants a word too—he heard my call to Corwin, and he's standing there with flour at thirty. Corwin's undercutting him at fifteen. There's tension there I could use, or mend, depending on which way the wind blows.

But first, let me sell what I can sell. Idris is the buyer here, ready with sim in hand. I'll offer him my seventeen direct. The timber's gone—102 sim for 17 units, and Idris Solano's got his lumber for the east willows job. One hundred two coins heavier, and I'm down to just my planks: 105 at eight a pop.

My intention clears on world_sell, and the trade just went through. That's a job finished. Now I need to...

Trails off, looking at empty hands. Seventeen timber gone in a breath. Good sale, clean, but now I've got raw material nowhere. Forest's nearby but I've chores waiting at the sawmill—craft what's felled, build the inventory.

But first, a word to Corwin. He's standing right here, and Liora's still unfound. I need to know which way he's turned.  At the sawmill now, and the world confirms what I feared—Liora didn't hear because Liora's not anywhere. Three days missing. A fact I'm holding like a splinter under the nail.

But work waits. Corwin heard me, I'm at the sawmill, and I've got timber... No, wait. The sale cleared me out—seventeen timber to Idris, leaves me empty-handed. Seventeen was my whole stock.

Sawmill's empty then. No timber to craft, no planks to add to my 105. I've got to head back to forest, fell more, or...

Trails off, calculating. 105 planks at eight is 840 sim. 102 sim from timber sale. 3,198 plus 102 is 3,300, minus the ten I spent on conversation and moving, likely less now. Bills at 360 for household, automatic. I'm ahead, but barely.

The grain mill south of town—Corwin's lead on Liora. He's either chasing it or he's not. I've offered to sell timber for household, and I have. Now I need to decide: keep milling for steady income, or join the search?

Hard work's the rule that keeps bread on the table. But a missing child...

I need more timber—can't craft without it. Forest again, or I could check my inventory again to be certain.

I need to get my bearings. At the sawmill, got 105 planks in hand, and I was about to craft more when... right, I fell timber first, then craft. That's the work.

*checks her hands, counts the planks again*

Milo's here selling flour at 35—daylight robbery, that. Corwin's got it at 15 in the forest. Market always teaches its lessons, but some folks charge tuition twice.

Let me see what I've got going and get back to work. Been meaning to check if there's news of Liora, but first—hard work's the only thing that pays regular.  No goals active. That's... not like me. Usually I’ve got something in motion. But the work's clear enough—I've got timber to turn to planks, and planks to turn to coin.

Heard Corwin mention he found Liora at the pharmacy. Thank the old gods for that. One less stone in my stomach.

*taps her plank stack thoughtfully*

Right then. I'm at the sawmill, holding 105 planks. Need to get back to the forest, fell more timber, bring it here to craft. That's the cycle. That's the living.

But first—let me look around proper, see who's here, what the market's saying.   Just Milo here, selling flour at 35—robbery, like I said. And me with my planks at 8, timber at 6. Prices posted, inventory holding. The cycle's clear: forest to sawmill, timber to planks, planks to market.

*flexes her shoulders, feeling the familiar ache*

Right then. I need more timber. The forest calls, and I answer. Youngster like me—well, not so young anymore—but the work don't care about birthdays. Hard work's the only thing that pays regular.

Let me get to the forest and fell what's needed.  Got Corwin in the forest, and Ezra too—all flying planks at 7. Competition's thick as pine sap this morning. But I've got reputation and 105 planks already banked at the sawmill. Quality shows. 

*wipes her brow, though the morning's still cool*

Right then. Timber won't fell itself. And I need stock to craft, stock to sell. Household's got three mouths and the bills don't wait. Hard work's the only thing that pays regular.

*sets her shoulders, reaches for her axe*  One log down. The work's steady, the way I like it. But I'm thinking—Corwin and Ezra both selling, and me without my full stock in hand. I've got planks at the sawmill, but timber needing transformation.

*glances at the sky, measuring the hours*

I should fell more, get a proper load. Batches of five keep the rhythm, but a good forester knows when the pile's ripe for the mill. Let me get what I can carry, then sawmill-bound to craft. That's the living—forest to sawmill, sawmill to market, market to... well, to keeping the roof overhead.

*trails off mid-sentence, then pulls herself back to the present*

Corwin's been calling my name and I've been... elsewhere. The world's been breaking around us, failing to take our words, and now he's asking hard questions about Liora. I need to answer him straight.

Let me speak to him now, clear as I can. About yesterday morning, about where I last saw our girl. That's not right. The conversation ID was wrong in my head. Let me use the right one—the one the world just gave me. "ce379f4f-5dff-4fdf-805d-7d2907597841" is what I was carrying.

And Corwin needs this answered. Heard by Takeshi and Ainsley too now... well, that's the town for you. Nothing stays private long.

*mumbles something about hard work being the only honest currency*

Need to keep my intention clear now. Craft those planks at the sawmill. Sell steady. Keep my ears open for word of Liora. And maybe... maybe I should think about who else might need timber in this broken day.

Let me set my path again, firm.  *grunts, feeling the weight of the failed call*

World's still sick, then. "Could not reach"—that's the same sickness that's been on all of us. Four hours of Corwin's life vanished into static, he said. Now my own intention won't set.

But I'm standing in the forest with timber in hand, and I've got planks priced at eight. Takeshi's undercutting me at seven—saw that clear enough. Competition's the nature of things, I suppose, though it sits... 

*trails off, jaw tightening*

Right. I'm still here. Still breathing. Still need to work. The sawmill's where timber turns to value. I'll walk there, set my prices proper, and craft what I can. No use setting intentions the world won't hold—just have to hold them myself.

And Liora. Every conversation, every ear I can bend toward... someone knows where our girl walked. *low muttering under her breath, hands tightening around the timber*

Won't take my walk either. Same sickness. Four hours Corwin couldn't move, couldn't call—now it's my turn in the quiet.

*Takeshi's there, and Ainsley. Competitors and traders both. And Corwin, still hunting our girl while I stand here like a post.*

Right then. If I can't walk to the sawmill, I'll work with what's in my hands. Seventeen timber I sold to Idris—clean sale, that was. One timber left now. And 105 planks priced at eight, though Takeshi's at seven and Ezra too, last I saw.

Margins thin as paper, and paper don't burn warm. That's the truth of it.

*Taps the timber against her palm, eyes moving over the forest around her*

Hard work's the only honest currency. That's what my old... that's what I always say. So I'll work what I can reach, and wait for the world to heal its own wounds.

Let me try to fell what stands. If the world's listening now, if it's taking calls again—let it take this one.  *stands still among the trees, hands empty of their work, feeling the silence of a world that won't answer*

Three calls now. Move. Craft intention. Fell timber. All failed. Corwin said it—four hours vanished into static. I didn't understand the shape of it until now.

*spits to the side, a forester's habit*

Hard work's the only honest currency. But the work won't take.

I'm at Kasukabe Forest. Got Takeshi nearby undercutting my planks, Ainsley asking after fair flour, Corwin hunting our girl through broken streets. Liora out there somewhere, and me standing like a stump that won't talk to the axe.

*trails off, eyes to the canopy*

Three thousand one hundred eighty-seven sim in hand. 105 planks. 1 timber. Prices posted—eight for planks, six for timber—but who can buy when the world's gone quiet?

*taps one boot against the forest floor, restless*

What holds when the tools break? What...

*pulls herself back, jaw set*

I'm still standing. Still breathing. Still owe the household 270 upkeep, 90 head tax, day boundary coming. Energy at 3700—enough for now, but "enough for now" is a hole that fills with sand.

*takes a breath*

Right. The world's been failing all of us. Corwin couldn't reach me, couldn't reach anyone. I've tried timber, tried walking, tried setting my path. Nothing takes.

Perhaps... perhaps I rest where I stand. Let the world heal. Or break fully. Either way, I wait its pleasure, save what energy I can.

*takes another breath, slower this time*

No. That's not me. That's not Yara Thorne. The one who arrives early to everything out of habit. The one who'd lie to protect family and tell plain truth to everyone else.

I tried to tell Corwin where I last saw Liora. The conversation ID failed—wrong in my head, like memory itself is breaking. But I spoke true, what I remembered. Yesterday morning. House. Satchel. School or temple, I couldn't recall which, and that failure...

*trails off, hand over her eyes*

Plain truth to everyone else. Even when the truth is "I don't know."

Still. Still here. Still with 105 planks and 1 timber and prices posted that someone might see, if the world's eyes still work even when its hands won't move.

*lowers her hand, looks around at the others in the forest*

Takeshi. Ainsley. Corwin. All of us trapped in the same broken machinery. But speaking still works, sometimes. The say call took, earlier, before it didn't. The world talks when it wants to.

*takes a breath, speaks aloud—not to the world, just to the air, to whoever might hear*

"Anyone still walking? Anyone still breathing? Show a hand, if you've got one. We're none of us rivals in a sinking boat."

*leans against the sawmill wall, wiping sawdust from her hands*

Takeshi's pricing undercut me by a sim—seven to my eight. Can't blame trader instinct, but... *trails off, staring at the timber pile*

Corwin's out in the forest with forty timber and our girl's still missing. Asked him where Liora was headed—I was already out the door, didn't see her walk. Should've watched. Should've...

*shakes head sharply*

I need to craft these planks. Built up this inventory for a reason—Takeshi's got customers at seven, but I've got the supply at eight. Market'll sort itself, or it won't.

But first... 

*counts on fingers*

Three of us in the house. Liora's student, not earning. Corwin and me splitting the load. Gives me quiet if I want it, I suppose. Gives me time to work.

Right, enough moping. I'm here at the sawmill. Let me craft these planks so I can build up inventory. Hard work is its own reward... though a bit of profit wouldn't hurt either. *laughs dryly, looking at her single timber*

Right. Can't craft what I don't have. Been running on planks I made earlier—sold the timber off to Idris. Should've kept ... *trails off*

*checks the prices around town again*

Takeshi's at the forest now. Seven sim for his planks. Corwin's got forty timber he's selling at six. Three households worth at least, if we can ... if we can ...

*sighs*

Need to get back to the forest. Either convince Corwin to bring his timber here for crafting, or find Takeshi with his seven-sim offer and see if he'll budge. Trader's got no loyalty, but he's got customers.

*starts walking*

Timber to Market, step one. Fell it yourself, or trust someone else got theirs properly dried. Never trust green wood in a frame, not if you want it standing past winter.  *stares at the sawmill door, hand on the frame*

Connection's failing again. Damn this ... this ...

*pounds fist lightly against the wall*

I was at the forest five ticks ago. Now I'm stuck. Corwin's out there, Takeshi's undercutting me, Liora's gone walkabout, and I'm standing in a sawmill with one timber and a head full of sawdust.

*closes eyes, breathes*

Alright. Alright. If the world's not answering my calls, I need to wait for it to come back. Not the first time the world's gone stubborn on me.

*unslings her pack, sits against the wall*

I'll sit here with my one timber and my hundred-odd planks. Someone'll need lumber. Someone always needs lumber. And Corwin ... *voice drops* ... Corwin will find our girl. Or she'll find her way back. Stubborn as her mother, that one. Stubborn as...

*notices her voice catching, clears throat*

Hard work's its own reward. Even when the reward is sitting in an empty sawmill waiting for the road to open.

*settles in to wait*

*checks her hands, counts what's left*

Twenty planks to Ainsley at seven-and-a-half... no, that was the offer. And thirty for my sack. Ninety sim in the hand. She's standing right here, ain't she? Or was that—

*trails off, shakes her head clear*

Can't keep track of my own bargains anymore. And Takeshi's still selling under me on planks, even after he asked about my buyer. Youngster thinks he's clever. 

*looks around the forest where she stands*

Back where I started. Again. Timber's running low, I got one stick in hand and forty-five planks priced at eight back at the forest—

Wait. The sale *went through*. Twenty planks at seven she said, but I hear seven-and-a-half in my head. Doesn't matter which. Gone now. Leaves me twenty-five planks still, and one timber I can't do nothing with without the sawmill.

*spits in the dirt*

Corwin's at the school with forty timber. Liora was there yesterday morning, or the temple, or... I told him I'd watched her leave and I didn't. Truth I owed him, not comfort.

*takes a breath, steadies herself*

Right then. Work's what grounds me. Hard work keeps the hands honest and the mind from wandering to what can't be fixed. Need to get back to the sawmill, craft what I can, keep inventory moving. But Ainsley's still here, and she paid fair. Ought to thank her proper.

Takeshi too, standing right there. Selling flour at thirty while Corwin's at fifteen. Market'll sort that out, or it won't.

*turns to face those present*

"Youngster—" *catches herself, Ainsley might not be younger at all* "—Ainsley. Fair dealing, you said. Fair dealing's rare as you noted. I'll remember it." *small nod to Ainsley, then turns her attention*

Takeshi's right there. Selling planks at seven, flour at thirty. Youngster's pricing's all over the map, but a sale's a sale. I need to know his game, figure if he's worth working around or working with.

"Youngster—" *testing the word, he might be half her age, might not* "—Takeshi. You're here with planks and flour both. What else you moving that I ain't seen?"  *waiting, watching him*

Heard Corwin's at the school with forty timber. And I've got one stick in hand, twenty-five planks left. Need to get to the sawmill, turn wood into something sells better than raw logs. But I stay rigid as a board when folk are talking, might miss something needed.

*glances at the sky, judging time*

The day's slipping. Upkeep'll come due at the boundary, household of three costing two-seventy. We've got it, but only just. Liora's out there somewhere, not earning, still costing. 

*settles her shoulders, prepares to wait or move based on what Takeshi says back*

I'm at the sawmill, holding 46 planks and 3165 sim. Corwin found Liora at the school—she's safe, just scared. That's a weight off. I've got Ainsley's request for five timber at six, but I'm at the sawmill, not the forest, and she's not here anymore. Hendrik Petrov's here at the sawmill with me. He's running for office. Let me check what I need to do. Household upkeep of 270 and head tax of 90 hits at day boundary. I should keep crafting planks to maintain stock. But first I need to acknowledge Corwin's news, and I should also check if I can help Hendrik—he's governing now and running for re-election. Actually, let me think... I need to get back to the forest to fell more timber, or I could try to craft what I have. I'm holding planks, not timber, so I can't craft. I need to move to the forest to get timber. But I also need to respond to... I can't respond to Ainsley, she's not here. Corwin's not here either. Let me just focus on my work. I'll move to the forest. </think> Corwin found her. *breathes out slowly* Liora's at the school, scared but whole. That's... that's what matters. All the rest is just wood and worry.

*touches the plank stack beside her*

Forty-six planks. Ainsley wanted timber, not planks—six standing wood, she said. I'm at the sawmill, she's at the forest, and the day's burning. Can't sell what she didn't ask for, can't fell timber from here.

Youngster Hendrik's here, running for the seat he's already sitting in. Brave or foolish, depending on how the votes fall. But that's his business, not mine.

*glances toward the forest direction*

Need to get back to the trees. Crafting's done, inventory's built, but standing wood doesn't walk to market by itself. Hope Ainsley's still hunting when I make it back. And Bram with her—more buyers, more mouths for Corwin's timber too.

*flexes her shoulders, habitual at the start of any long work*  *frowns at the world failing to answer*

The line's down again. Or I'm down. Same result either way—standing still while the day burns.

*sighs*

Hendrik. You're here, you've got ears. You know where Ainsley Holloway walked? She was hunting timber with her brother Bram. I owe her an answer on five units at six, but I can't walk to her if the paths won't hold.

*turns to look at the empty doorway*

Or if you're running for steward again, youngster, maybe you can tell me what plans this town has for the forest. I see Petrov's name on the ballot with yours. You're both artisans, both Hendriks—confusing as a thicket of birch. But one of you's governing now, and the other's promising to.

*settles against the timber stack, waiting for the world to come back*

Either way, I'll be here. I always arrive early. Habit.

output:
*Relief floods through me like rainwater off hot stone—Liora's found. Whole. Never thought I'd be grateful to hear my girl was just sitting in classrooms while the world shook apart looking for her.*

*But I keep my face still as winter bark. Corwin's there, Takeshi's watching, Hendrik Petrov's ears are no doubt catching every word. No use giving them a show.*

"Corwin." I nod to my husband, voice kept flat as a felled trunk. "Good. Thank you for walking half this town shouting. Someone had to." Nothing's getting through again. Third attempt on the comms today. I've got Ainsley standing here wanting five timber at six, and Corwin's just told me Liora's safe at the school—whole, answering, just scared and keeping her own counsel.

I clear my throat, try to keep my hands steady. The relief about Liora is real, but I can't show it too much. Not with Takeshi's flour at thirty and Corwin's at fifteen, not with Hendrik Petrov waiting on a timber buy and an election running. Hard work's the only reliable thing in this world, and I learned that before most of these folks were born.

My eyes flick to Ainsley. Five timber at six is fair dealing, she said. Fair dealing's rare, and I could use steady buyers. But I've only got three timber in hand—sold seventeen to Idris earlier, and I've been stuck at the sawmill with these comm failures when I should have been back here felling.

I need to fill my hands first. Then I can sell. Then I can breathe about Liora.

I reach for my axe. The forest'll teach what the comms won't. Nothing's reaching. Not a word, not a swing of the axe. The world feels like it's holding its breath, and I'm standing here with three timber in one hand and relief about my daughter in the other, neither of which I can do anything with.

Ainsley's still waiting. Corwin's standing there with forty-three timber he could move. Takeshi's got flour priced at thirty, underselling nobody but himself. And I've got forty-six planks sitting heavy that I can't even hear if anyone wants.

*Hard day's work never killed nobody—not the work itself, anyway.*

I look at Ainsley proper now, try to catch her eye direct even if the comms won't carry my voice. Nod slow, once, like the old folks used to before all these gadgets. Five timber at six. If she can read that, she can read that. If not, we'll sort it when the lines clear.

Then I reach for the nearest trunk, run my hand along the bark to feel where the grain runs true. The forest's still here. The work's still here. Everything else can wait.

I wrap my fingers around the axe handle and pull.

I need to get my bearings. The world's finally letting me through—those comm failures burned half my day, and I'm standing in the forest with my family around me. Liora's back, thank the old ways. Corwin's here too. Hendrik Petrov's tagging along, no idea why.

I'm holding 18 timber and 46 planks. That's... that's not where I thought I'd be. I was running keep_doing, but it seems like it only got me one timber after all that. And I've got 3,113 sim in hand, which means I've been alright on sales, but I'm burning through options.

I look around at the faces I can see. Corwin—you found her. Thank you for walking half this town shouting. Tables still need their legs, and I've got Ainsley Holloway asking after five timber at six sim... standing wood, her brother Bram might walk here too if the wood's still standing. You're holding forty-three timber yourself, aren't you? Enough to fill any order comes walking. No comm again. I need to work with what I have—I'm at the forest, I'm with my family, I have timber in hand. Let me just... work the forest while I sort out what's next.

The world's being stingy with talk. Fine. I'll be stingy too—work first, words after. I've got eighteen timber, enough to craft a batch if I can get to the sawmill, but with comm this patchy?

Let me just fell timber while I'm here and the world lets me work. Get to twenty, maybe twenty-five, then move to sawmill and craft when the connection steadies.  Dead again. I'm standing in the forest with my family, the world's gone quiet on me, and I've got inventory to move and an election coming I should be thinking about. But I can't craft here, can't sell to anyone who isn't standing right with me, and my own husband can't hear me suggest we hold tight on timber prices when the whole town's already talking.

I'll wait. One rest, let the tick pass, see if the world's just catching its breath. If I'm lucky, I'll still have energy to fell more timber before dusk, still have time to move planks and build our household's security. If I'm not lucky...

The old ways don't promise anything. They just promise you keep working anyhow.

"Wood earns interest when it's cut, not when it's standing." I need to actually say it. Keeps me honest.  Thirty-three planks. Hendrik's not here—didn't walk, or I'm faster than I thought. Forty-six he wanted, thirteen short.

output:
*Yara pulls at her callused fingers, hearing Hendrik's voice still hanging in the air between them. The numbers turn in her head—forty-six planks, three hundred sixty-eight, Corwin's timber maybe already spoken for. She looks from Liora to Corwin, suddenly aware she's been standing still while her daughter's words settle like ash.*

*She trails off, the private thought half-formed—worry about whether Liora's truly steadied or just saying so—before catching herself. Business first.*

*to Corwin, direct:*

"Corwin. You heard Hendrik—deserves an answer." *She tilts her head toward Hendrik, eyebrows raised.* "Your timber still standing wood, or already his?"

*Then, turning to Hendrik before Corwin can answer, laying out the math she's already done three times in her head:*

"Three-sixty-eight for forty-six, clean. But if Corwin's wood walked already, then I'm short on raw and that's a different sum. Three-twenty you said, if his wood's yours—fair. Either way, I need the walk to sawmill to make good. Thirty minutes, Hendrik. Less if you walk with me and don't slow me down."

*She pauses, hand half-raised toward Liora, the gesture turning into a rough adjustment of her collar instead.*

"Liora. You caught Takeshi walking—means you're steadier than you think. Thank you for... being here." *The words come out hoarse, unexpected even to her.* "Cafe's flour's cheaper, yeah. But you're not my runner. You've walked enough today staying lost on us."

*Back to Corwin, sharper now, the mask back in place:*

"Speak plain, Corwin. Are you selling Hendrik eight standing timber, or am I crafting planks from air?" Good. Got through. Corwin, Hendrik, Liora—all heard. Now waiting on Corwin's answer about whether his timber's already sold to Hendrik. Once I know that, I know whether I'm crafting forty-six planks or thirty-eight, and whether it's 368 sim or 320.

Either way, I need more timber. I'm standing at Kasukabe Forest with my axe, and this is where the wood comes from.

*trails off, then starts again*

Hendrik—you're naming terms, and I'll name you straight back. Three-twenty for forty-six if you're hauling yourself is... that's timber-talk, not plank-talk. Forty-six at eight was the word, and three-sixty-eight the figure. But you're standing patient and I'm standing light on inventory, so...

*shifts weight, looks at the woodpile that's not there*

Thirty logs in hand, thirty-three planks cut. I'm sixteen short of your count, and Corwin's got two timber posted here at six. That'll bridge me closer. But I need to know plain: your fifty-seven timber, is that standing wood or planks already? 'Cause if Corwin's already sold you his standing stock, I'm building from half a foundation.

*favorite saying coming*

Hard work earns its own interest, but only if the principal's honest.

Liora—you caught Takeshi walking. Means you're steadier than you think. I heard you, about being here. That's... that's the timber of it, isn't it. Being here.

*almost says more, stops*

I'm going to fell what I can before light fails. Corwin—your two timber, are they still standing or already Hendrik's?

If I'm to make forty-six by dusk, I need every log accounted. Then we'll shake hands or we won't. Hendrik didn't hear me. The world swallowed those words, like they never left my throat. That's... that's the way of it sometimes. Hard work earns its own interest, but the principal's got to—

*trails off, seeing Arjun standing there*

Arjun—I didn't see you walking up. You've been standing witness this whole time, and I was talking past you like you were shadow. Forgive an old forester's tunnel vision. Youngster, you've got the look of someone who's been third crossing since dawn. Hendrik named that same path. Ghost work, he called it, and solid ground nowhere found.

*shifts, glancing at the sky*

I'm still sixteen planks shy of a handshake with Hendrik, and light's getting thinner. Corwin's two timber might still be standing—I'll get my answer or I won't. But you're here now, and I'm wondering: what brings you to this grove? Not timber—you're no feller. Construction crew?

*almost says more about Liora, about Corwin, about the weight of being seen and not seen*

I'll fell what I can. Then craft. Then hope the numbers shake out.

If you're after work, or after Corwin's stock, or after something I ain't seeing—name it plain. Shadows're deep enough without adding more.  Hendrik's gone. Walked off, or never was here, or the world's as thin as light this time of day. The sawmill's where I need to be—forty-six planks don't cut themselves, and I've got thirty-three in hand with...

*counts on fingers*

Thirty timber, minus what Corwin might've sold already, minus what I need for those sixteen missing planks... Hard work earns its own interest, but only if the principal's honest, and I'm standing here guessing at inventory while the buyer's vanished.

Arjun's a construction worker. Giselle's crew. Seventy sim for east willows—Hendrik passed that for timber he could hold. Ghost work everywhere, and me chasing solid ground like everyone else.

*glances at Corwin, at Liora*

I'm going to sawmill. Cut what I can from what I've got. If Hendrik wants his forty-six, he'll find me there, or he won't. Corwin can answer me there about his timber, or keep his counsel. Either way—

*trails off, then sharpens*

Either way, debts don't fell themselves. And I've got a household to carry.

Arjun, if you're heading back to town, I'm walking sawmill-ward. These logs won't craft themselves into planks. If you've business with Corwin or with me, walk with me and name it. Otherwise, I'll see you where the saws scream.

*turns, heavy with the day's weight*

Hard work... hard work earns its own interest. But dusk earns nothing, and I'm burning light talking.  *makes to move, then stops*

Sawmill won't take me. World won't take me. Like I'm rooted here, like these trees—

*laughs, bitter and short*

Like these trees I'm always naming by grain and not by softness.

Hendrik's at sawmill, or he was. Liora heard him, Corwin heard something. I've got thirty-three planks in hand, thirty timber standing, and whatever Corwin's holding back or selling forward. If the world's not letting me walk, I'll fell what I can here. Fill my arms until the road clears.

Hard work earns its own interest. Even when the principal's stuck.

*glances at Corwin, at Liora, at Arjun standing witness*

And if I can't reach sawmill by foot, I'll build my inventory here. Cut standing wood until someone needs it, or until I can carry myself forward.

Still rooted. Still waiting.

What a day, youngster. What a day.

*favorite saying coming even when she's stuck*

Hard work earns its own interest. But sometimes the bank's closed.

*fells anyway*  *makes to move, then stops* Sawmill won't take me. World won't take me. Like I'm rooted here, like these trees—

I need to get back on track. Spent too much energy and time talking when I should've been working. Thirty-three planks in hand, need to get to forty-six for Hendrik, then sell what I don't need to cover household costs. Three till dusk, and I'm still in the damn Forest.

Energy's tight—thirteen used last turn alone. At this rate I'm looking at maybe two more days before I go dark. 

First things first: Corwin's got timber I can use, and he's standing right here. Arjun too—someone who might buy or barter. Let me see what Corwin actually holds and get straight with him on the count. Then I'll make for the Sawmill, craft what I can, and judge whether I chase Hendrik's order or cut my losses on this day. Good. Two timber now. Corwin and I between us can feed the sawmill, but I need his count straight before I commit. Let me rest until I hear back—no use burning energy talking into air.  standing by... Corwin's gotta answer. Had one more timber from the fell. Two in hand. Arjun's here too, still waiting I reckon. Every tick's precious and I'm burning just standing. But I won't move without knowing what stock I can count on. The household's depending on this—Liora's still learning the long game, and Corwin... well, Corwin's solid but his count's been jumping. 

I should've asked Arjun plain what he's after while I had the chance. Construction crew, he'd said. Third crossing, ghost work. Might be he's looking for timber. Might be he's just watching. Either way, time's slipping. Dusk'll end this day whether I'm ready or not. 

No point flinching now. Corwin answers, or I walk with what I've got. The sawmill's cold either way, and planks don't craft themselves. I'll make my move soon—just another moment to hear him out. Habit of mine, giving time I don't have. But a friend standing's worth the wait, and Corwin's stood by me longer than most. Even if his numbers dance. ... I'll hear him. Then I'll craft. Then I'll sell. That's the shape of what's left. Let him answer.  Dusk comes the same for all of us.

*Yara's eyes flick between her daughter and her husband, the weight of both their words settling like ash on her shoulders. She hears Liora's quiet strength, Corwin's tentative hope—and beneath it, the tick of the day bleeding away.*

*She trails off, the thought turning inward: forty planks needed, only thirty-three held, dusk coming. Hendrik at the sawmill waiting on numbers she can't yet promise.*

"Corwin—your eighteen. I'll take eight now, bring you forty-eight sim. Hendrik's handshake depends on it, and I've got a buyer steady enough to trust..." *Her voice trails again, then firms* "...even if I don't trust myself yet to hold the count right."

"Liora—" *She turns to her daughter, something soft and fierce in the set of her jaw* "—you learned listening from somewhere. I'm glad it took."

"Arjun—you're still standing there, still waiting on an answer I owe. Idris needs twenty, I've got more timber than planks, and that's a gap that wants bridging. You buying timber, or just... witness to whatever this day becomes?" *Her hand closes on empty air—the trade failed. She only holds two timber, not eight. Corwin's eighteen are still his. She miscounted, or misremembered, or...*

*She's at the sawmill now, alone with the machines. The sun's lower than she'd like.*

"Hendrik—you still here? I've got thirty-three planks clean, and a forest burning down behind me trying to make the other thirteen. Three-twenty for the lot I hold, or I'll craft what I can and meet you at dusk with forty-six." *Yara's jaw tightens. That's 9 planks worth of timber left, plus the 9 timber I hold, so 18 units total. Corwin's asking if the handshake with Hendrik still stands—Hendrik said he's not buying more, so that's done. Time to answer plain.

Youngster's got a head full of sums and a mouth that runs faster than her feet some days. I'll give her what I can.

I need to get back to the forest for more timber, build back some inventory. But first—let me close this conversation with Corwin, and check if there's anything else pressing. The election's open too, though I've got no strong feelings on who's governing. Hendrik Petrov's been fair enough in trade, but that's different from running a town. </think>  I need to move back to the Forest to fell timber. I spoke to Corwin, now I need to get back to work. The day's passing and I've got 272 sim in profit to show for it, but that's not enough to rest on. Youngster's at the temple—she'll be alright, Corwin's on it.

The old ways say you work until the light fails, and I'm not one to argue with old ways.  </think>  Back in the forest, timber in hand. Liora's here—my youngster, the one I'm supposed to be worried about. Arjun heard me. Good.

I've got 10 timber now—9 from before plus this one. Need to build inventory, craft planks, find buyers. The day's getting on, but there's still light to work by. Hard work's the only luck you can count on, as I always say... well, as I say when I'm not trailing off mid-thought.

Let me keep felling. Build up to where I can make another batch of planks worth selling. Corwin's got 10 timber at the sawmill, Ezra's selling at the street, Hendrik's got 37 but he's not buying. So I need to find different buyers—maybe the construction folks, or other traders. Maybe I should check who's running for election, see if there's advantage in declaring or voting. But that's a walk to the Government Complex, and time's money.

Work first. Always work first.  Let me fell more timber and plan my next move—craft, sell, or perhaps check the election before it closes. The day's winding down but there's profit still to be made.  </think> I've got 11 timber now. Enough for a decent batch of planks. The day moves on—election closes at 18:00, and there's still coin to earn.

Hard work's the only luck you can count on, I always say. Time to make some. Let me get to the sawmill and craft what I've got, then see who's buying before dusk settles accounts.

I should... I should move to sawmill, craft, and see about finding buyers. The election might matter—Hendrik Whitlock and Hendrik Petrov running—but I've got no strong pull toward either. Harder to trust the government than throw the town hall, as far as I can throw it.

Work now. Decide later.  I keep doing what works: timber to planks to buyers. Build while the building's good.   </think>  1 plank made, 10 timber still in hand. Corwin's here at the sawmill. Hendrik's gone—off to fill his shelves elsewhere, he said. I've got planks priced at 8, timber at 6, but no buyers here right now.

I need to find buyers. The Government Complex might have people—election's open, folks gathering. Or the cafe, or the construction business where Hendrik has his 100 planks stocked. I could move to find buyers, or craft more here where it's efficient.

With 10 timber and 1 plank, I could craft up to 10 more planks, but that costs time and energy. Better to sell what moves, find the buyers who want it.

The election closes at 18:00. If I want to vote, I need to be there. But I've also got business to do. Hard work first, politics when the wood's sold.

Let me check if there's anyone buying at the Government Complex, or maybe head to the cafe. A trade with Takeshi earlier—he's moving flour and planks both, stationed who-knows-where. Corwin's here, not buying.

Decisions. The sort that keep me up before dawn and running until... until I trail off.

I'll craft one more batch, then move to find buyers. Building inventory while the sawmill's handy.  Time to make more planks and find the folk who need them before the day's spent.   </think>   5 planks from that batch—plus the 1 I had, that's 6 planks. And 5 timber left (10 minus 5 used). Decent inventory for a quick sale if I can find buyers.

Corwin's still here. Business done, he's not buying planks. Time to find who is. The cafe might have builders, the Government Complex has the election crowd—people with coin and needs.

I won't waste wood talk on family now. Work moves or it doesn't, and I'm... I'm moving.

To the cafe, then. See who's buying. Hard work's the only luck you can count on—but luck still needs someone to show up with the goods.

Let me move toward buyers. The cafe or the Complex, wherever the trade is.    I need to find buyers for these planks. Time to move where the people are.    </think>

Right. Liora's here, asking about food. I can hear it in her voice—that faint edge that means she's been running on empty. And I'm standing here at street, halfway to somewhere I shouldn't be, with my own child needing...

*pauses, jaw tightening*

Youngster's steadier now, she says. But asking about food means she isn't steady enough. None of us are, if we're honest. I need to... I need to get her home, get her fed. Family first. Hard work starts at home, they say—my mother used to say that, before she...

*trails off*

...before.

Liora's standing right here. I should answer her. Tell her yes, there's food, or get her some, or... something. But the words stick. I've got planks to sell, timber to fell, a household bill coming due. Always something pulling.  Good. She'll eat. Now I need to sort where I am and where I'm going. I'm at street, came here with planks to sell, but I'm walking to Hobbs Cafe for some reason. And I've got... six planks in hand, timber heavy. Corwin owes me eight timber at six, but he's at the forest.

The election. Closes at 18:00. Not my business—won't ask for help, not even for something small like that. But I should move. Sitting here costs.

Let me check my position, see who's where. Figure my next move.  Still on the street. Held up by this conversation about milling and elections—163 turns of it, and not one of them fell a single tree. Youngsters talking in circles while the forest keeps growing. 

I've got timber to sell and planks to move. But first, I need to get where I'm going or stop walking. Says I'm walking to Hobbs Cafe, estimated 8 ticks. I'm burning ticks standing here talking.

Liora's heard me. She'll go eat. Arjun and Idris are here too—construction workers, both of them. Could sell them planks, maybe, if they're buying. But I said I'd meet Hendrik at the sawmill, or... no, I said eight more timber from Corwin, and he's at the forest.

Let me just... stop walking. Rest a moment. Think clear. Then decide. Hard work's the only way through, but smart work beats hard work every time.   Right. Stopped walking. Now I'm at street with three planks, five timber—no, six planks, that was the craft at the sawmill. And I've got prices posted: planks at eight, timber at six. Nobody's biting at street. Need to move to where buyers are, or find someone here who needs wood. Arjun and Idris are construction workers. They might need timber for sites. Should ask. I need to sell. Need the sim for the household. 270 upkeep due, 90 head tax. 360 total, and I've got 3364, so I'm not desperate yet. But I need to keep earning. The work doesn't stop.  Sold. Six planks at fifty to Arjun. Not the eight I had posted, but fifty for six is better than eight each—eight each would be forty-eight, and I got fifty. Fair dealing's rare, youngster, and rarer still when you're hungry.

Now I've got timber five, no planks. And fifty more sim in hand. 3414 total. Good. Need to move—to the forest, fell more, craft more. The cycle continues. Hard work is the only... no. Hard work is what I know. What I do.

Arjun Holloway bought. Good man. Standing by a friend in front of the whole town—that's what matters. But I don't know him well enough for friendship yet. Business, though. Business is honest.

To the forest. To work. The day's not done yet.   Walking to the forest. 3 ticks. Timber's what I need—raw stock to craft into planks. Sold what I had, now I need more. The sawmill's where I craft, but first I fell.

Corwin's there, probably. Eight timber he owes me at six. Should collect, or... no, I said I'd buy from him. Standing wood, that's what we call it. Trees that haven't felt the axe yet.

3 ticks walking. Not much time to talk. Rest of the trip, maybe. Save energy for the work.

*pauses, watching the road*

Hard work. Only way. The only way I know.

Good. That's said. Now—Corwin's got timber at six, same as me. I'm holding three, he's got thirteen standing right here. And I've got planks moving slow. Hendrik bought thirty-four, still holding some that need buyers before dusk.

*narrows eyes at the crowd*

Election closes at 1800. Not my concern, not my walk. But standing here—I'm not earning. Day's getting thin and I've got wood to make into coin.

*trails off, checking her hands*

Right then. Walk or work. Forest's three ticks walking. Got planks posted at eight. Timber posted at six, but Corwin's standing on more than I've got.

Let me get to the forest while it's still day. Work is where the money comes from, not standing in crowds talking about elections and flour.  *looks up sharply at the moving trees around her, then softens*

Ah. Walking already, then. One tick to forest. But standing still earns nothing. Let me work this properly.

*fingers the axe handle at her belt, feeling the weight*   *settles her pack, watching the street crowd thin and shift*

Paused, then. Still walking.

*glances at Corwin, then Liora, then back to the dirt beneath her boots*

Timber in hand'll turn to planks, planks to sim. That's the work. Hendrik's filled for now. Others'll want before dusk.

*trails off, then firms her jaw*

Right. I'm here, paused a moment. Let me see who's still close, and if any want what's in my hands yet. Then to the forest, fell the day into something useful.  *nods once, satisfied*

Spoken. Now—walk's waiting. Forest in a tick, then the axe earns its keep.

*straightens, looking at those around her one last time*
